<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/auth/organization/remove-member (route, the route ledger binds it to client method organizations.removeMember), /api/v1/auth/organization/update-member-role (route, the route ledger binds it to client method organizations.updateMemberRole))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via cloudManaged (symbol, a field of const object PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via createOrganization (symbol, a field of const object CLOUD_MANAGED_REFUSAL_MESSAGES), createOrganization (literal, a string literal in CLOUD_MANAGED_MEMBERSHIP_DOORS; a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `36a7f3b0efbf401a1fc54efd24b6d7e2c3175dc0` — the merge of head `852c9a0e942bfc395181fa9739dd889144632c35` into base `f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 36a7f3b0efbf401a1fc54efd24b6d7e2c3175dc0 && git checkout 36a7f3b0efbf401a1fc54efd24b6d7e2c3175dc0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082 852c9a0e942bfc395181fa9739dd889144632c35 && git checkout -B drift-repro f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082 && git merge --no-ff 852c9a0e942bfc395181fa9739dd889144632c35

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `def9a07ea55e9e23340908f182d52d06c2ac07d8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/cloud-managed-visibility.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/action-predicate-sparse-face.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/platform-objects.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/membership-required-every-posture.dogfood.test.ts; read, not reviewed: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, organization-add-member.ts, auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts, auth-plugin.ts, packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts and sys-invitation.object.ts

Read at 2026-11-16T03:48Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6906689819; lane request 6906680880 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented in a project thread for security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff was judged against the merge base with `main` (12 files, +307/−11), not against the merge commits.
- The two refused doors hold as claimed. The refusal keys on the endpoint's declared path alone, so it does not depend on the body; it sits ahead of the remove-member permission arm and ahead of the role-change grant read, and it throws before the vendor handler. No in-process caller of either vendor operation exists outside those two routes. The tests pin envelope, unchanged rows and both arms not called, each with a self-hosted control in which the arm does run.
- One predicate: every reader goes through `isCloudManaged()` in `@objectstack/core`; this diff adds no second reading of the switch.
- `sys_member` stays read-only through the data API (`apiMethods` get and list), unchanged here, so the object door is not a second route to the two refused writes.
- `visible` is declared as a hide, not as enforcement: the changeset, the object comments and the registry comment each say the door refuses and the action is hidden. `gatedInputs` gains three paths; the guard's forward rows read them and the walker floor moves 37 to 40, the reverse direction is unchanged. The lowering matrix and the sparse-face sweep read the new conjunct.
- Self-hosted is unchanged and pinned (three 200 controls that change the row).
- The exception is, in code, exactly the platform-administrator gate on exactly `add-member`; this diff does not widen it.
- The declaration's census is not closed. See M1.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@objectstack/spec` is the level the repo rule gives a non-protocol breaking change; the BREAKING banner, the who-moves sentence and the ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, `no-migration-prescription`) are present and the marker's reason is true: nothing stored is rewritten. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is well-formed and matches PR body and changeset. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true although a spec file changed: the hunk adds three entries to a feature-flag registry list, no authorable key, accepted value or metadata type moves, and the author reports the generated artifacts up to date. `Skills-docs: none` reason read and accepted.

CI at this head: 73 check-runs, 23 success, 16 skipped, 33 in progress (Test Core, Test UI, Build Core, Build Docs, type-check and lint lanes), 1 cancelled (`Check Changeset`). Nothing has failed yet; nothing is settled either. The cancelled changeset check needs a re-run on the next head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security-touching (authentication, membership). Mechanisms and the per-door reading are kept out of this record and are with the seat.
- BREAKING narrowing, hosted environments only.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — the declared rule is wider than the doors the change closes, and the declaration says otherwise. The rule as written: on a cloud-managed environment the hosting organisation decides who is a member and at which tier. The change refuses two doors and states, in three places (`cloud-managed.ts` module comment, `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`, the changeset), that these are the two doors that change an existing membership and that `add-member` is the one door left open. Read against the organization family in `auth-route-ledger.ts`, that census is incomplete: further ledgered routes write or delete a membership row and carry neither a cloud-managed disposition nor an out-of-scope sentence, and no pin holds them either way. Required: give every organization-family route that creates, ends or re-tiers a membership an explicit disposition on a managed environment (refused with the same envelope and a pin plus control, or open by rule with its reason written down), bring the row actions and `gatedInputs` into line for any door that becomes refused, and make the three sentences true to the result. Either direction closes this; an unstated remainder does not.

S1 (should-fix) — the exception is described by its purpose (restoring a membership the environment lost) while the page's lead sentence says the hosting organisation decides membership and tier. The open door is not bounded by that purpose in code. State on the docs page what the door admits on a managed environment, or bound it; and add to the new describe a pin that the door refuses a caller who is not a platform administrator on a managed environment, so "exactly the platform administrator" is held where the exception is claimed.

N1 (nit) — the invitation refusal has a second line behind the hook; the two new refusals have one. A sentence in the hook comment saying so, and why one suffices today, would keep the next in-process caller from walking past it.

Held against the published spec on `main`: the registry entries make the hide real in both guard directions and take no declared capability from a self-hosted consumer.

Independence: implemented in a project thread for security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

### ① Derived judgments

- Delta: one commit since `def9a07e` (6 files, +232/−28), no merge. The whole diff was re-read against the merge base; the findings below are about what that one commit left behind.
- Prior M1, code side: closed. The refusal now covers six organization-family doors (remove-member, update-member-role with Make Owner, leave, accept-invitation, create, delete) through one arm that keys on the endpoint's declared path alone, answers the invite-member envelope, and sits ahead of every authorization arm and every write for those paths. Each of the four new doors has a pin (rows unchanged, nothing created, the invitation still pending) and a self-hosted control in which the door does write. The rest of the family is open by a written rule in the `cloud-managed.ts` header (it writes no membership row), with one control. No in-process caller of the six vendor operations exists; the object door stays read-only for memberships and invitations.
- Prior M1, declaration side: not closed. Of the three sentences only the module header was corrected. See M1.
- Row actions and `gatedInputs`: the four actions behind the new doors carry the conjunct and are booked, so the guard's forward direction resolves. Their pins did not move with them. See M2.
- Prior S1: the pin is there (a caller without platform-administrator standing is refused at add-member on a managed environment, nothing written). The admission is now stated in the module header, not on the docs page. See S1.
- Prior N1: closed. The hook comment says this is the only line, why one suffices today, and what a future in-process caller owes.
- One predicate still: the delta adds no second reading of the switch.
- No new door is opened. Self-hosted is unchanged and pinned (five further 200 controls). The platform administrator's add-member path is untouched.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on the three packages remains the level the repo rule gives a non-protocol breaking change, and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is well-formed. `Metadata-protocol: none` is still true after the second spec hunk: four more entries and a notes sentence in a feature-flag registry list; no authorable key, accepted value or metadata type moves. The ADR-0087 marker's conclusion still holds (nothing stored is rewritten), but its reason text and the rest of the declaration describe the previous head. See M1.

CI at this head: 65 check-runs, 28 success, 10 skipped, 27 in progress (Test Core 1 to 8, Test UI 1 to 16, Type Check workspace, Type Check UI, Build and E2E UI). Nothing has failed yet and nothing is settled. By reading, M2 predicts a red Test Core lane.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security-touching (authentication, membership). Mechanisms and the per-door reading are kept out of this record and are with the seat.
- BREAKING narrowing, hosted environments only, now six doors and seven hidden actions rather than two and three.
- For the maintainer's eye, not a finding: with create and accept-invitation refused, a person who holds no membership on a managed environment has no way in from inside it except the platform administrator's add-member or the hosting organisation. That follows from the rule as ruled; it is worth one sentence on the docs page so it reads as intended.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix, continues prior M1) — the declaration no longer matches the change, now in the other direction. The code refuses six doors and hides seven actions; the changeset (title, the `Clause-②` narrowed list, the BREAKING paragraph, who-moves, the ADR-0087 marker's reason), the PR body and `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` still name two doors, three actions, three registry paths and two refusal sentences. Four breaking refusals (leave, accept-invitation, create, delete) would ship with no release note and no who-moves line for the member who leaves, the invitee who accepts, or the owner who creates or deletes an organization. The docs page still says "the two doors that change an existing membership", which was the sentence prior M1 asked to be made true. Required: bring the changeset, the PR body and the docs paragraph to the six doors, the seven actions, the family rule for what stays open, and who moves for each.

M2 (must-fix, new) — the pins for the hide did not follow the four new gates. The lowering matrix in `platform-objects.test.ts` still pins the previous predicates for `create_organization`, `delete_organization` and `leave_organization` byte for byte, while this head authors a cloud-managed conjunct on each; read against the sibling rows, those three rows cannot hold at this head (not run locally; Test Core is still in progress). `accept_invitation` has no row there, and `cloud-managed-visibility.test.ts` still holds only the three `sys_member` actions: none of the four new hides is pinned as hidden when managed, offered as before when not, and still under its other gate. Required: correct the three rows, add the fourth, and extend the visibility describe to the four actions with their controls.

S1 (should-fix, continues prior S1) — the pin half is done. The docs page still describes the open door by its purpose alone; say there what it admits on a managed environment (who may call it and what it may add), as the module header now does, or bound it in code.

N1 (nit, new) — `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` still says 40 booked inputs and floors at 40; 44 are booked now.

Held against the published spec on `main`: the narrowing takes nothing from a self-hosted consumer and makes the registry's hide real for the four new actions at the door; what fails is that the release declaration and the predicate pins describe a smaller change than the one in the tree.
